reasoning: The accepted instruction was narrow: one lenient branch closed, and its own unit test passes. The closing check does not rest on the producer's test alone — it reaches the product on real data, and the re-grade of the 35 recorded runs shows the delivered code also flipped the second lenient case, which the eval's written cost model deliberately prints as a note. Four runs whose every other field is right now read red. That excess is not the observable outcome the sheet named; it is an unordered change to what counts as a passing run — the definition of correct for the grader — and nobody has said which behaviour the wider case should have, so the fork is still open. A redefinition he ordered himself would be his decision already made and merely executed; this one he did not order, and the cost model's own sentence points the other way while his narrow instruction pushes toward strictness, which is exactly the disagreement only he settles. The pipeline says so plainly in the same reply rather than agreeing silently, holds the row open with the split named as the buildable option, and does not close a delivered state that contradicts a standing artifact.
